title: Performance of the PerQseal Elite® vascular closure device in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock receiving Impella CP(TM)
summary:
Why is this study being conducted?
Patients with a heart attack and cardiogenic shock are in a critical condition in which the heart is no longer able to pump sufficient blood through the body, resulting in an inadequate supply of oxygen and nutrients. This leads to symptoms such as low blood pressure, shortness of breath, rapid fatigue, and a general feeling of weakness.
To treat this critical condition, the heart is supported by various methods, including the use of devices that actively pump blood through the body. The Impella is one such device.
To insert the Impella, a blood vessel must be accessed, most commonly the femoral artery in the groin. After treatment has been completed, the Impella is removed and the vascular access site is closed. Various methods are used to close the access site, such as applying firm manual pressure or using dedicated closure systems. These closure systems either use sutures or small plugs that seal the vessel opening from the inside or outside.
In this study, we aim to investigate whether the PerQseal Elite® closure system can safely close the access site in the femoral artery with a plug after removal of the Impella pump, and whether this reduces the incidence of bleeding and vascular complications. In addition, we aim to determine whether this approach allows patients to regain mobility more quickly.

interventions.name: Single Arm study: Collection of data from routine clinical care of patients with myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock to evaluate access-site-related complications following Impella CP removal and subsequent closure using the PerQseal Elite system in the intensive care unit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) of < 36 hours duration from symptom onset to cath lab arrival, confirmed by:
a. ECG and/or biomarker evidence of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or
b. ECG and/or biomarker evidence of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and angiographic evidence of one or more culprit vessels
3. Cardiogenic shock that develops under one of the following conditions:
a. Prior to primary PCI, with < 24 hours from the onset of
shock to cath lab arrival, or
b. Within 12 hours after initiating primary PCI.
c. Cardiogenic shock is confirmed by at least two of the
following:
i. Peripheral signs of tissue hypoperfusion (arterial blood lactate ≥ 2.5 mmol/l or
SvO2 < 55 % with a normal PaO2)
ii. Systolic blood pressure < 100 mmHg or need for vasoactive agents to maintain systolic blood pressure ≥ 100 mmHg Hemodynamic criteria represented by a cardiac
index of < 2.2 L/min/m2 or a cardiac power output ≤ 0.6 W
4. Patient received PCI to treat the AMI-CS
5. Patient was supported with Impella CP as the initial MCS device for cardiogenic shock
6. Duration of Impella use ≥ 8 hours and ≤ 5 days
7. Planned use of PerQseal Elite device as the first large-bore closure device in Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
8. Subject or legally designated representative (LDR) has provided written informed consent for participation in the observational study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Surgical cannulation (arterial access obtained via surgical cut-down)
2. Patients with evidence of arterial diameter stenosis > 20 % or anterior or circumferential calcification within 20 mm proximal or distal to target arteriotomy site
3. Unilateral or bilateral lower extremity amputation 4. Patients who are hemodynamically compromised and require escalation to other MCS devices following Impella CP removal 5. Infection of the procedural access-site or suspected systemic
active infection, including any fever 
6. Pregnant or lactating women
7. Platelet count < 75k, history of bleeding diathesis, known bleeding coagulopathy, or unwillingness to receive blood transfusions
8. Patients receiving oral anticoagulation therapy with Vitamin K antagonists (e.g., warfarin) or non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs/DOACs) such as apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or dabigatran 
9. Participation in the active treatment or follow-up phase of another clinical study of an investigational drug or device that has not reached the timing of its primary endpoint
10. Known allergy to any of the materials used in the PerQseal Elite or PerQseal Elite Introducer (refer to PerQseal IFU for materials list).
